title: qar-rule-upload input file
description: The JSON array upload-rules.sh reads. Each entry becomes one POST body for {base-url}/rules/v1/rule, whose request model is qodo-platform's RuleCreateRequest (operationId create_rule_rules_v1_rule_post). This schema describes the file as written, not the wire body: it also allows the snake_case example aliases and the mixed-case severity the script normalises before sending. A file that validates here passes the script's own validation, and a file that fails here is rejected by the script before the first request.

rule.title: rule
rule.description: One rule. The six contract fields are mandatory; scopes is the only optional one the script forwards. Any other field (sourceType, state, ruleId, createdAt, ...) is accepted here and dropped with a note before the POST, so a GET response can be round-tripped back into an upload unedited.

name.description: Concise rule name, unique in the workspace - a duplicate comes back as HTTP 409. Max 128 characters (RuleCreateRequest.name).

category.description: Rule category. The API accepts any non-empty string, so a typo here quietly creates a new category rather than failing; GET /rules/v1/metadata lists the ones a workspace already uses.

content.description: What the rule checks or enforces, 1-3 sentences, imperative voice.

goodExamples.description: Code that FOLLOWS the rule. May be "", but the key must be present - as goodExamples or as good_examples.

badExamples.description: Code that VIOLATES the rule. May be "", but the key must be present - as badExamples or as bad_examples.

good_examples.description: snake_case alias for goodExamples, renamed by the script before the POST.

bad_examples.description: snake_case alias for badExamples, renamed by the script before the POST.

allOf.$comment: goodExamples or its alias must be present; the platform requires the key even when the value is empty.
badExamples or its alias must be present.

nonBlankString.description: A string carrying at least one non-whitespace character. The script trims before checking, so "" and "   " are both rejected.

severity.title: severity
severity.description: RuleSeverity: error = must comply; warning = comply by default; recommendation = apply when appropriate. The script lowercases and trims, so "Error" and " WARNING " are accepted in the file and sent as "error" and "warning".

examples.title: examples
examples.description: A code snippet as a single string. Empty is allowed; a list or an object is not.

scopes.title: scopes
scopes.description: Repository paths the rule applies to, e.g. "/owner/repo/" or "/owner/repo/src/module/". Max 100 (RuleCreateRequest.scopes maxItems). Omit the key for the universal scope "/"; [] is accepted and normalised to "/" by the platform. Entries are trimmed, and a bare string is wrapped into a one-element list.

anyOf.title: a single path, wrapped into a list by the script

anyOf.$comment: A non-empty list needs at least one non-blank entry; blank ones are dropped.
